evidence.claim: The bank's model scored the flagged transaction 0.90. That is the reason this alert exists, not a finding. It carries no weight in this assessment: across the 5,565 closed cases every cleared alert scored 0.82 or higher, so the score records which alerts were opened, not which were fraud.
The customer has 32 prior transactions, median amount $68.48. The flagged $1,000.03 is 14.6x that median.
Card C10434-K1 carried 1 transaction(s) in the 48 hours to the alert (1 in the last 24). Its own prior 30 days average 0.1 per 48 hours, so this window runs +0.9 against the card's own rhythm.

The identity record marks this device as New for the account (id_15 = New). This is the single strongest counter-indicator in the closed cases: the cleared alerts are dominated by cardholders confirming a purchase from a new phone. A new device alone does not support a block.
The flagged transaction stands alone on this card in the 48-hour window.

A single transaction 14.6x the customer's median with no change in card activity around it. In the closed cases this shape is repeatedly a cardholder confirming an unusually large but intended purchase.
Retrieved 6 confirmed-fraud and 0 cleared investigations closed before this alert, reached through this customer or a shared device profile. A prior verdict does not transfer.

The same device profile appears on 36 other customer(s) in the prior 30 days. A DeviceProfile is DeviceInfo, OS, browser and screen combined; common handsets collide, so sharing one is a lead, not identity.

Every transaction carries a `risk_score` between 0 and 1 from the bank's detection model. The model is useful and imperfect: many high scores are legitimate, and some fraud scores low. A score is a reason to look, never a verdict. The only confirmed outcomes are in the closed cases.
Case CC-0657: model scored a $1,769.94 transaction at 0.90. Cardholder confirmed the purchase. Amount unusual for this customer but consistent with their stated intent. Alert cleared.
Case CC-3761: model scored a $3,891.01 transaction at 0.89. Cardholder confirmed the purchase. Amount unusual for this customer but consistent with their stated intent. Alert cleared.

case.summary: Alert HHG-010 opened on 2016-12-02 from a risk score on transaction 3506725 ($1,000.03, online) for card C10434-K1. The findings that moved the assessment most: The identity record marks this device as New for the account (id_15 = New); A single transaction 14.6x the customer's median with no change in card activity around it. Card activity ran at 1 transaction(s) in 48 hours against a 0.14 baseline for this card. 6 closed investigation(s) reachable from this customer or its device profile were retrieved as memory, 6 of them confirmed fraud. The evidence supports legitimate activity at probability 0.04; no transaction is treated as part of a fraud episode.

sar.reason: Policy 3a: a report is required only when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected and exposure exceeds $1,000, the activity connects to a shared device profile or region cluster, or the pattern is coordinated or undocumented. This case is assessed legitimate at 0.04 with $0.00 exposure and 0 connected card(s), so none of those conditions is met and the internal case alone is the correct record.
